pr.title: Add Ghostty setup and a mosh example to the README and site
pr.head: f92f683df6c90c460e22049ffcb80754235306f2

summary: trip keeps terminal sessions alive in a background daemon, and a terminal tab is a client that attaches to one. The README and the trip.here page explain how to set up a terminal so that every new tab starts in trip. Before this change they covered macOS Terminal and iTerm2 only.
This pull request changes documentation only, in two places:

1. Ghostty setup. Ghostty is configured through a text file, not a settings window. The change gives two lines for that file: command = ~/.local/bin/trip enter, which starts every new tab in trip, and confirm-close-surface = false, which stops Ghostty from asking before it closes a tab. Closing a tab only detaches from the session, so the prompt protects nothing. The text names the reload key for both macOS and Linux.
  2. Remote sessions over mosh. mosh is a remote shell that survives sleep and network changes. The new section gives one command that runs trip on another machine, and it explains why each part of the command is there: -- so mosh stops reading options, sh -c so ~ expands, and TRIP_DETACH_KEY="^]" so the remote trip doesn't compete with a local trip for Ctrl-\. The README also covers the mosh-server path on a Homebrew Mac and keeping 24-bit color.

The first head used Ctrl+- for the remote trip. Ghostty on Linux, and other Linux terminals, take that key to shrink the font, so the second head switched to Ctrl-], which those terminals leave alone. The review's finding about that is fixed. A third head shows where the Homebrew --server option goes in the command, and the head is signed off.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Detach key: the keystroke trip intercepts to open its session chooser. A second press detaches. The default is Ctrl-\, and TRIP_DETACH_KEY changes it.
  • Surface: Ghostty's name for one terminal, such as a tab or a split.
  • mosh-server: the program mosh starts on the remote machine over SSH. It runs the command you give mosh.
  • CSI u: an escape-sequence spelling of a keystroke, which a program can ask the terminal to use. trip recognizes a detach key in that spelling too.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• 8346a52: one finding: Ghostty on Linux binds Ctrl+- to shrink the font. There were three suggestions: the Homebrew path, the Linux reload key, and wrapping.
  • 0a33457: the key changed to Ctrl-], and all three suggestions were taken. The review was clean, with one new suggestion: show where --server goes in the command.
  • f92f683: the Homebrew sentence now shows the full command, with --server before the host and before --. An incremental review found it clean.

groups.title: README: Ghostty setup and the mosh section
groups.kicker: The full text that readers copy commands from
intro: The README carries every detail. The Ghostty subsection sits under Terminal setup, beside the macOS Terminal and iTerm2 entries. The new Remote sessions with mosh section follows Switching and detaching, because its key advice builds on TRIP_DETACH_KEY, which that section introduces.

Read the commands and config lines as code: a reader pastes them as they are. Prose around them explains each choice, so a reader can adapt the command, for example to another detach key or another host.

files.note: Adds the Ghostty subsection and the mosh section, including the Homebrew mosh-server path and 24-bit color.

checks.text: Ghostty 1.4.0's own docs (ghostty +show-config --default --docs) say that a command with arguments runs through /bin/sh -c and applies to every new surface, and that confirm-close-surface = false closes surfaces without asking. Its default keybinds put reload_config on super+shift+, on macOS and ctrl+shift+, on Linux. +validate-config accepts both config lines at this head.

mosh 1.4.0 parses options in Getopt::Long's default mode, so the -- is what stops it from reading -c as an option of its own. It passes the command to mosh-server new ... --, which runs it without a shell. Under sh and dash, a variable assigned before exec reaches the program.

The Homebrew command puts --server before the host and before --. Run through mosh 1.4.0 with a stand-in ssh that logs its arguments, it starts /opt/homebrew/bin/mosh-server new ... -- sh -c '...' with the quoted string intact across the line break.

parse_detach_key("^]") returns 0x1d, Ghostty's ctrlSeq sends Ctrl-] as 29, and encodes_control accepts the CSI-u form, code 93. Ghostty binds no plain Ctrl-] on either platform, and mosh's own escape key is Ctrl-^.
trip passes the client's COLORTERM into a session when it creates one and again on each attach, through the trip env shell hook. That's why setting it on mosh-server is enough.

groups.title: trip.here page: the short version
groups.kicker: The same two additions in the page's own markup
intro: The page adds a Ghostty entry to its setup list and a new Remote sessions with mosh section. It reuses the README's wording but leaves out the Homebrew and color details. A new pre.snippet style shows config lines and commands in the page's terminal colors, which the page defines for both its light and dark themes.
The new section follows the page's existing pattern of a section labeled by its h2. The only new external reference is a link to mosh.org.

files.note: Adds the pre.snippet style, the Ghostty entry in the setup list, and the mosh section.

checks.text: The reload keys match the README: Cmd+Shift+, on macOS and Ctrl+Shift+, on Linux.
The remote key is Ctrl-], the same as in the README's command.
